sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Sector breadth is extremely narrow with only Technology maintaining an all-green profile, while Real Estate and Industrials lead short-term deteriorations.

Technology and Healthcare continue to dominate sustained performance, holding top-tier momentum scores of 0.933 and 0.800 respectively. While Energy maintains the top YTD spot (rank 1) with solid 0.683 momentum, short-term improvements are marginal and limited to single-spot advances across Healthcare, Financials, and Communication Services.

Meanwhile, rate-sensitive and cyclical sectors remain deeply suppressed. Real Estate dropped 2 spots over the last five sessions to rank 9, sitting alongside Utilities (0.217) and Consumer Cyclical (0.233) at the bottom of the momentum curve.

## Strength
- **Narrow Market Breadth:** Only 1 of 11 sectors (Technology) is all-green across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD timeframes.
- **Sustained Leadership:** Technology (momentum 0.933, rank 2) and Healthcare (momentum 0.800, rank 4) are the sole sectors maintaining top-3 ranks across 1-, 3-, and 6-month windows.
- **Top Absolute Rank:** Energy preserves the #1 YTD rank with an above-average momentum score of 0.683.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Top 5-Day Improvers:** Communication Services (+1 to rank 8, momentum 0.67), Financials (+1 to rank 7, momentum 0.48), and Healthcare (+1 to rank 4, momentum 0.80).
- **Steepest Slips:** Real Estate declined 2 spots over five sessions to rank 9, while Industrials slipped 1 spot to rank 5 (momentum 0.533).
- **Momentum Anchors:** Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.233, rank 11), Utilities (momentum 0.217, rank 10), and Real Estate (momentum 0.200, rank 9) form the bottom tier.

## Divergences
- **YTD Rank vs. Momentum Disconnect:** Basic Materials holds a high YTD standing at rank 3 despite sluggish momentum of 0.417.
- **Lagging Position Despite Momentum:** Communication Services has built momentum up to 0.667, yet its overall placement remains depressed at rank 8.

rotation_phase.label: Mid Cycle
rotation_phase.reasoning: Technology is the dominant leader alongside strong Industrials momentum, which fits a mid-cycle expansion despite defensive Healthcare strength.

risk_radar.relative_strength: Technology is the sole sector genuinely beating the S&P 500, posting a perfect rs_score of 1.00, an rs_confirmed of 1.00, and beating SPY across 7/7 timeframes. No other sectors display sustained outperformance, and no RS new highs or crosses are reported in the data.
risk_radar.risks:
- Crowded leadership is concentrated entirely in Technology, as it stands alone with an rs_score of 1.00 while all other evaluated sectors beat SPY on 3 or fewer of the 7 timeframes.
- Both Energy and Healthcare show fading follow-through, with their rs_scores of 0.50 (beating SPY on 3/7 timeframes) dropping sharply to an rs_confirmed of just 0.17 due to weak directional consistency.
- Communication Services shows early weakness, beating SPY on only 3/7 timeframes with an rs_score of 0.33 deteriorating to an rs_confirmed of 0.11.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Breadth remains exceptionally narrow with only 8 of 144 groups all-green, led by sustained strength in Energy, Tech, and Healthcare, while retail and domestic cyclicals show aggressive short-term rotation.

Leadership is anchored by high-conviction pockets: Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.964) and Semiconductors (momentum 0.925) dominate broader trends, reinforced by persistent multi-month strength in Computer Hardware (0.893) and Marine Shipping (0.893). Simultaneously, short-term momentum is rotating into consumer and real estate pockets, evidenced by sharp multi-spot advances in Department Stores (+21 spots) and Real Estate - Diversified (+18 spots).

Conversely, basic materials and precious metals are fading rapidly. Gold dropped 15 spots to rank 64, while Paper & Paper Products shed 20 spots to rank 114. Capital-intensive and financing laggards remain deeply impaired at the bottom of the market, with Gambling (0.023), Mortgage Finance (0.038), and Advertising Agencies (0.076) exhibiting near-zero momentum.

## Strength
- **Narrow all-green breadth:** Only 8 of 144 industry groups are positive across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD timeframes.
- **Top momentum leadership:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing leads the market (momentum 0.964, rank YTD 2), closely trailed by Semiconductors (0.925, rank YTD 7) and Diagnostics & Research (0.922, rank YTD 31).
- **Sustained intermediate leaders:** Computer Hardware (0.893 momentum, rank YTD 1) and Marine Shipping (0.893 momentum, rank YTD 6) continue to hold top-36 positions across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons alongside Diagnostics & Research and Semiconductors.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Sharpest 5-day advances:** Department Stores jumped +21 spots (rank 59, momentum 0.84), Real Estate - Diversified surged +18 spots (rank 72, momentum 0.74), and Health Information Services climbed +14 spots (rank 24, momentum 0.85).
- **Sharpest 5-day declines:** Paper & Paper Products fell -20 spots (rank 114, momentum 0.38), Gold lost -15 spots (rank 64, momentum 0.46), and Confectioners dropped -14 spots (rank 70, momentum 0.34).
- **Persistent laggards:** Absolute momentum remains worst in Gambling (0.023, rank YTD 143), Mortgage Finance (0.038, rank YTD 142), Advertising Agencies (0.076, rank YTD 144), REIT - Mortgage (0.090, rank YTD 128), and Solar (0.092, rank YTD 138).

## Divergences
- **Fading cyclicals:** Steel (momentum 0.71, rank -3 in 5d), Specialty Industrial Machinery (momentum 0.62, rank -4 in 5d), and Staffing & Employment Services (momentum 0.62, rank -1 in 5d) show high overall momentum that is beginning to lose 5-day rank.
- **Emerging low-momentum movers:** Early rank surges are appearing in otherwise weak momentum profiles, led by Luxury Goods (+13 spots, momentum 0.45), Grocery Stores (+9 spots, momentum 0.47), and Apparel Manufacturing (+9 spots, momentum 0.42).

industries.watchlist:
- Airlines - RS cross watch; confirm if relative strength sustains above the zero line against SPY on expanding volume, while a quick slip back into negative relative territory invalidates the rotation trigger.
- Apparel Retail - RS new high trigger; confirm if relative strength breaks out to hold fresh 20-session highs relative to the broader market, whereas failure to sustain the high and an immediate pullback below the prior breakout level invalidates the leadership signal.
- Luxury Goods - Emerging rotation watch; confirm if the recent 5-day rank jump (+13) and positive acceleration (+0.06) lift momentum above 0.50, whereas stalling rank and rolling over into negative acceleration invalidates the move.
- Specialty Industrial Machinery - Fading momentum watch; confirm downside vulnerability if the 5-day rank drop (-4) continues to deteriorate despite high absolute momentum (0.62), while a sharp rebound in rank order and renewed relative upside invalidates the fade thesis.
